2611.17431.title: Quantum violation of Causal Friendliness in the instrumental scenario
2611.17431.abstract: How far can quantum theory depart from a classical worldview? Bell inequality violations show that no theory can simultaneously uphold absoluteness of observed events, freedom of choice, relativistic causality, and classical causal explanations. While generalized notions of causality, capable of incorporating quantum resources, can account for Bell correlations, the Local Friendliness theorem showed that, in extended Wigner's friend scenarios, the conflict between quantum theory and causal explanations persists even after classical causality is abandoned. This revealed a new form of nonclassicality stronger than what was revealed by Bell's theorem. However, Local Friendliness has been confined to Bell causal structures so far, and it remains unknown whether a related form of nonclassicality persists in more general causal networks. Here we answer this question by considering a Wigner's friend version of the instrumental network, a paradigmatic causal structure in which communication between parties is allowed, and, unlike the Bell scenario, relativistic causality does not impose any restriction. We show, both theoretically and in a proof-of-principle photonic experiment, that quantum correlations are incompatible with Causal Friendliness, which is the conjunction of the absoluteness of observed events and the generalized nonclassical causal constraints imposed by the network. Such constraints extend relativistic causality from Bell scenarios to networks of arbitrary structure. These results establish a form of quantum nonclassicality stronger than previously observed in instrumental-network violations of classical causality, generalizing Local Friendliness beyond Bell-Wigner scenarios and uncovering a new class of correlations with potential applications in future quantum technologies.
2611.17431.why: Extends Local Friendliness beyond Bell structures: a Wigner's-friend instrumental scenario shows quantum violation of 'Causal Friendliness'.

eli5.plain: They show that the clash between quantum theory and 'observed events are real for everyone' survives in a broader class of cause-and-effect setups than Bell tests.
eli5.how: Embedding friends who measure inside an instrumental causal network, they derive inequalities from absoluteness of events plus causal assumptions and find quantum violations.
eli5.matters: It widens where observer-dependence of facts bites, giving new targets for Wigner's-friend style experiments with photons or qubits as 'friends'.
eli5.caveat: Like Local Friendliness, it relies on treating a quantum system as an observer; the experimental bite depends on that contested premise.

2611.12481.title: Universal two-qubit control across dilution refrigerators via a 10-km coherent optical link
2611.12481.abstract: Distributed quantum networks are important for scalable quantum processors and for potential applications in communication, distributed computation, and sensing, in which direct classical links for adaptive control are essential to harness the shared entanglement. However, controlling superconducting quantum processors from a separate refrigerator over long distances remains elusive. Here, we introduce a coherent optical link (COL) that delivers microwave waveforms and their phase references between dilution refrigerators. Combining a laser, a microwave-to-optical transducer and an optical-to-microwave photodiode, the COL transmits microwave control signals over 10~km of fiber, while optical references derived from the same laser compensate for the frequency mismatch between devices. Through the COL, we deliver a universal gate set to a transmon qubit and a cavity qubit in another refrigerator and entangle them, and achieve a Bell-state fidelity of 80.6\%. Quantum control delivered through the COL thus provides a classical backbone for modular quantum processors.
2611.12481.why: Drives a universal two-qubit gate set on a transmon and cavity in another fridge over 10 km fibre via microwave-optical transduction.

eli5.plain: They controlled qubits in one refrigerator using signals sent as light over 10 km of fibre from another location.
eli5.how: A laser carries microwave waveforms through a transducer and photodiode, and optical references from the same laser lock the frequencies of both ends.
eli5.matters: Remote, phase-coherent control is a prerequisite for distributed superconducting processors and microwave quantum networks.
eli5.caveat: It transmits classical control, not quantum states; gate fidelities and added noise versus local control need scrutiny.

2611.13665.title: Observation of strong electric dipole-dipole interactions between two atoms
2611.13665.abstract: We have prepared pairs of atoms at densities exceeding $ 10^{16}/\rm{cm}^3$ corresponding to $n\lambdabar^3>10$ and studied how they interact with light. In this regime, the coherent part of the electric dipole-dipole interaction is larger than the dissipative part, and a single photon emission can transfer large momenta (larger than ten times the single photon recoil) to the atoms. For off-resonant laser light, the atoms are dressed with an electric dipole moment of $\approx$ 1 Debye and interact coherently. This light-induced dipole-dipole interaction has been previously observed only in the far-field mean-field regime. For two atoms, the resonance is shifted by the two-body Lamb shift which is dominated by the near-field part of the dipolar interaction. Dipolar resonance shifts have been observed before only for many atoms interacting with the far-field part of the dipolar interaction. Our work sheds new light on photoassociation processes and paves the way for studying driven quantum systems with strong electric dipole-dipole interactions.
2611.13665.why: Two atoms at near-field separations show coherent dipole-dipole coupling exceeding dissipation, a measured two-body Lamb shift and large photon-recoil momenta.

eli5.plain: They pushed two atoms so close that their light-induced dipoles talk mainly through the near field, and measured the resulting energy shift directly.
eli5.how: At densities where interatomic distance is below the reduced wavelength, off-resonant light dresses atoms with dipoles; the pair resonance shifts by the near-field two-body Lamb shift.
eli5.matters: This is the minimal 'two emitters at sub-wavelength spacing' system that waveguide and giant-atom circuits emulate; it gives an optical benchmark for coherent versus dissipative exchange.
eli5.caveat: Two-atom statistics and density control are hard; detailed comparison with theory relies on modelling of the trap and motion.

2611.14484.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor
2611.14484.abstract: Electric flux strings underpin confinement in gauge theories. In two spatial dimensions, their evolution involves competing processes of charge motion, pair creation, and transverse deformation. Accessing these dynamics beyond perturbative limits challenges classical approaches, as entanglement growth restricts the times accessible to tensor-network simulations. Here we use quantum simulation to investigate a (2+1)D Z2 lattice gauge theory with dynamical matter and an explicit magnetic plaquette interaction, spanning strongly confined and nonperturbative deconfined regimes. Using 63 superconducting qubits, including 12 ancillas, we evolve initially localized strings with static or dynamical endpoint charges. Spatially resolved measurements reveal rapid charge and flux spreading in the deconfined regime, enhanced matter occupation in the string interior near the pair-creation resonance, and suppressed spreading at strong electric fields. String-path occupations further probe transverse rearrangements between configurations connected by plaquette operations. Retaining separate matter and gauge degrees of freedom makes local Gauss-law constraints directly accessible for error detection. Combining these constraints with ancilla checks and noise rescaling, we measure dynamics in circuits containing up to 15 second-order Trotter steps. Our results establish quantum simulation as a practical approach to exploring nonperturbative string dynamics in two spatial dimensions, with gauge redundancy serving as an experimental resource.
2611.14484.why: 63 qubits simulate string breaking and spreading in a (2+1)D Z2 gauge theory with dynamical matter beyond tensor-network reach.

eli5.plain: They used a 63-qubit chip to watch flux strings between charges stretch, spread and break in a toy version of particle-physics confinement.
eli5.how: Qubits encode gauge fields and matter on a 2D lattice, with ancillas implementing plaquette terms; spatially resolved measurements track charge and flux over time.
eli5.matters: A flagship-scale analogue simulation on superconducting hardware, in a regime where classical simulation struggles.
eli5.caveat: Noise limits the times reached; 'beyond classical' claims depend on the tensor-network comparison chosen.

2611.17511.title: Non-ergodic Area Scaling of Andreev Transport in Al/AlO$_x$/Al Tunnel Junctions
2611.17511.abstract: State-of-the-art superconducting qubits rely on Al/AlO$_x$/Al Josephson junctions (JJs) as a nonlinear element with an ideal sinusoidal current-phase dependence, with its inductance set by the junction area and oxidation conditions. This idealization holds only if the many conduction channels through the amorphous AlO$_x$ barrier transmit weakly and almost identically. Here, we measure the second-order subgap Andreev current, which sets the second Josephson harmonic, in Al/AlO$_x$/Al JJs. For junction sizes relevant to qubits, we find that this current is dominated by $\lesssim 300$ effective channels whose transparencies exceed the ideal tunneling limit ($\lesssim 10^{-6}$) by orders of magnitude. For small and high-aspect-ratio junctions, increasing the junction size does not average out the effect of these high transparency channels but instead adds additional channels of even greater transparency. The trend inverts once both the width and length of the junction exceed a critical length scale, above which the effective transparency decreases with area. This non-ergodic scaling of the Andreev current is reproduced by simulations and attributed to non-self-averaging statistics of the transparency distribution, which arise from variations in oxide thickness. The effect is largely invisible to the normal-state conductance used to target the inductance and reveals unexpected geometric and size-related trade-offs for scaling superconducting qubit systems to large numbers of junctions.
2611.17511.why: Al/AlOx junctions carry a few hundred high-transparency channels that dominate the second Josephson harmonic and do not average out with size.

eli5.plain: The standard junction in transmons is not the uniform, weak tunnel barrier everyone models; a few hundred leaky spots dominate.
eli5.how: They measure the subgap Andreev current, which is sensitive to highly transparent channels, versus junction area and shape.
eli5.matters: Higher Josephson harmonics shift transmon spectra and gates; this pins their microscopic origin and shows larger junctions do not fix it.
eli5.caveat: Transport measurements infer channel statistics indirectly; the link to qubit-level errors is argued, not shown here.

2611.10615.title: Simulating the quantum switch with quantum circuits is impossible
2611.10615.abstract: The quantum switch is a higher-order transformation that combines input quantum channels in an indefinite causal order. Whether quantum circuits can simulate its action, and how many calls to the input channels such a simulation requires, are natural questions about the power of quantum control of causal order. In this work, we prove that no quantum circuit with classically controlled causal order can exactly and deterministically simulate the quantum switch for arbitrary input channels using any finite number of calls. This impossibility holds already for qubit channels and extends to the complete $r$-switch, which coherently controls all permutations of $r$ input channels. These results settle the question of exact deterministic circuit simulation of the quantum switch. They demonstrate that processes with indefinite causal order cannot, in general, be efficiently simulated in this setting even by quantum circuits with classically controlled causal order.
2611.10615.why: Proves no quantum circuit with classically controlled order can exactly and deterministically simulate the quantum switch with finitely many calls.

eli5.plain: A mathematical proof that ordinary step-by-step quantum circuits can never exactly reproduce the 'superposition of orders' device.
eli5.how: They show impossibility for arbitrary qubit channels and any finite number of calls, extending to switches over many channels.
eli5.matters: Settles whether indefinite causal order is genuinely beyond circuits, which matters for interpreting photonic switch experiments.
eli5.caveat: Exact and deterministic simulation only; approximate or probabilistic simulation is a separate question.

2611.14391.title: Implementing rapid reset of superconducting qubits with on-chip dissipation
2611.14391.abstract: Rapid and high-fidelity qubit reset is essential for quantum state initialization and quantum error correction. Conventional reset protocols for superconducting qubits often rely on dissipative elements connected to external circuitry, exposing qubits to thermal noise from higher-temperature environments. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a scalable approach to qubit reset and leakage removal over multiple transmon qubits using dedicated dissipation units comprising resonators coupled to on-chip resistive loads. This architecture provides Purcell protection while isolating the qubits from warmer external circuitry. We achieve a median reset time constant of approximately 48 ns for the $|g\rangle-|e\rangle$ transition, with an effective bath temperature of 30 mK. A 400-ns reset pulse yields residual excited-state populations of $0.29\%$ and $0.67\%$ for qubits initialized in $|g\rangle$ and $|e\rangle$, respectively. We further demonstrate efficient leakage removal from the $|f\rangle$ state, reducing its residual population to $0.51\%$. These results establish a simple, reproducible, and easy-to-integrate approach to dissipation engineering in superconducting quantum processors.
2611.14391.why: On-chip resistive dissipators reset transmons in ~48 ns time constants at 30 mK effective bath, without warm external lines.

eli5.plain: They built tiny on-chip resistors that pull qubits back to their ground state quickly while keeping them away from hot wiring.
eli5.how: Each qubit couples through a filter resonator to an on-chip resistive load, giving Purcell protection when idle and fast decay when tuned in.
eli5.matters: Fast, cold reset and leakage removal directly shorten error-correction cycles.
eli5.caveat: Residual excited population is 0.3–0.7% after 400 ns; scalability across a large chip is not yet shown.

2611.17941.title: Benchmarking superconducting quantum processors with percolating entanglement quality
2611.17941.abstract: The capability to create large entanglement resources is a key performance attribute of quantum processors, and the size of the resource is often used as a benchmark of processor scale. Recent graph-state experiments have reported entanglement clusters spanning entire chips with hundreds of qubits. However, cluster size alone does not capture the entanglement quality of individual couplings or differences in coupling topology. Here, we introduce percolating entanglement quality (PEQ), a topology-normalized benchmark based on conditional two-qubit negativity and a topology-specific bond-percolation threshold. As an experimental demonstration, we prepare a native graph state on a 64-qubit square-lattice superconducting processor with defects, identify a 52-qubit entanglement cluster, and evaluate the PEQ of the processor. Applying PEQ to previously reported chip-wide graph-state measurements on heavy-hex-lattice processors, we show that PEQ differs substantially among processors whose entanglement clusters span the entire chip. PEQ provides a single chip-wide score without selecting a best-performing qubit subset or path. This score allows processors with different coupling topologies to be compared on a common scale and can inform the design of coupling topologies for scalable chips.
2611.17941.why: Proposes a topology-normalised entanglement-quality benchmark and finds a 52-qubit cluster on a defective 64-qubit chip.

eli5.plain: They argue 'how big is your entangled cluster' is a poor benchmark and propose one that also counts how good each link is.
eli5.how: Conditional two-qubit negativity on each bond is compared to the percolation threshold of the chip's lattice to yield one quality number.
eli5.matters: Gives a fairer way to compare graph-state results across processors with different connectivity.
eli5.caveat: Another benchmark metric; its adoption and correlation with algorithmic performance are open.

2611.13465.title: Real-time spectral combs from delayed quantum feedback in multimode cavity QED
2611.13465.abstract: We study the time-dependent physical spectrum of light for a two-level atom coupled to a large, but discrete, number of modes of an electromagnetic cavity. Radiation emitted by the atom, placed at the center of the cavity, returns after the round-trip time $t_r$, re-excites it, and is re-emitted, producing a sequence of atomic population revivals. For a coupling approximately flat over the atomic linewidth, the emission dynamics reduces to a delay-differential equation of Bixon--Jortner type. Using its analytical solution in terms of Laguerre polynomials, we investigate how successive emission and reabsorption cycles shape the time-dependent spectrum. The physical spectrum exhibits revivals during which a transient frequency comb of spacing $2π/t_r$ develops. The comb results from the quantum interference between successive emission stages; its teeth sit not at the cavity modes but at the resonances of the effective two half-cavities created by the resonantly reflecting atom. The visibility scales as $e^{-Γt_r}$ with the filter bandwidth $Γ$, and at long times the comb converges to the dressed-mode spectrum, which we also obtain analytically in quantitative agreement with exact diagonalization. We show that the physical spectrum resolves the feedback phase, to which the atomic population is insensitive in the regime of well-separated emission stages, and provides additional frequency-resolved signatures of the atomic position. We discuss two feasible experimental implementations of our results with transmons (artificial atoms) coupled to microwave and surface-acoustic-wave resonators.
2611.13465.why: Delayed self-feedback in a multimode cavity yields transient frequency combs whose teeth sit between cavity modes, set by emission–reabsorption interference.

eli5.plain: An atom in a long cavity keeps re-absorbing its own echo, and the emitted light briefly develops a comb of evenly spaced colours.
eli5.how: Light leaves the atom, bounces off the far mirror and returns after a fixed round trip; an exact delay-equation solution tracks how each emission stage interferes with the previous one in the time-resolved spectrum.
eli5.matters: Long transmission-line resonators and giant-atom layouts with transmons reach exactly this delayed-feedback regime, so the comb is a concrete, checkable signature for a microwave experiment.
eli5.caveat: Pure theory with a flat-coupling approximation; the comb is transient and needs time-resolved spectroscopy with resolution better than the round-trip time.

2611.16229.title: Infinite or indefinite: the query cost of simulating the quantum switch
2611.16229.abstract: The quantum switch applies two operations in a coherent superposition of their causal orders and is a simple example of indefinite causal order. No quantum circuit that uses each operation once in a definite order can even describe it, yet photonic experiments have demonstrated its physical realization. We ask how many calls to the black-box operations a quantum computer in the circuit model needs to reproduce the switch. If one of the black boxes is known to be unitary, three calls suffice. For general channels on a $d$-dimensional system, we prove three results. In all three, circuits may use classical feed-forward and unlimited ancillary quantum memory. First, no finite number of calls suffices for exact simulation in the worst case. Second, approximation to any fixed error below $1/2$, measured in half the diamond norm, requires $Ω(d^{1/4})$ calls, exponential in the number of qubits. Third, an ordinary circuit can require exponentially many calls to obtain a single bit that the switch extracts with a few uses. We consider a device whose actual noise is dephasing in a fixed unknown basis and test it against a theoretical depolarizing model. The two channels have the same entanglement and average gate fidelities, so these figures alone do not distinguish them. At fixed noise strength, the quantum switch tells them apart with a number of device uses independent of $d$, whereas the circuit model requires $Ω(d^{1/16})$ calls. Noise characterization is needed for quantum error correction, and this gives a provable query advantage of the switch in a task relevant to practical quantum computing. We invite future work that extends such advantages to more practical computing tasks.
2611.16229.why: Shows exact switch simulation needs unbounded calls and approximation needs Ω(d^{1/4}) calls, though three suffice if one box is unitary.

eli5.plain: They count how many times a normal quantum computer must use two black boxes to fake running them in both orders at once.
eli5.how: Lower bounds via diamond-norm arguments for general channels, plus an explicit three-call construction when one box is unitary.
eli5.matters: Quantifies the gap between indefinite causal order and circuits, complementing the impossibility proof this week.
eli5.caveat: Worst-case bounds; typical channels in experiments may be cheaper to emulate.

2611.15871.title: Revealing Bell Nonlocality Does Not Require the Same Physical Measurement to be Performed Twice
2611.15871.abstract: Bell inequality violations, or Bell nonlocality for short, is not only central to testing the foundations of quantum physics but have also become an essential ingredient of numerous quantum information protocols, from quantum key distribution to the device-independent certification of randomness and secure communication. Existing analyses of Bell nonlocality assume that a small set of predefined measurement directions can be reproduced exactly. But what if these directions cannot be reproduced at all? This may happen for fundamental or technical reasons, such as variations in the measurement apparatus. Here we show that the violation of a Bell inequality remains possible and that it also retains its operational significance, even when the measurement directions never repeat. We experimentally confirm these results using polarization-entangled photons, detecting only one particle pair per randomly chosen analyzer direction. Our results establish the robustness of Bell inequality violations against imperfect measurement repeatability and further connect Bell tests with the broader framework of randomized measurements. Moreover, they extend quantum information protocols to settings with limited measurement control, including quantum device certification, communication complexity, and quantum cryptography.
2611.15871.why: Bell violation survives and keeps operational meaning when measurement settings never repeat, confirmed with one photon pair per setting.

eli5.plain: You can still show quantum nonlocality even if your measurement directions drift and are never exactly the same twice.
eli5.how: They derive a test that works with randomly varying settings, then check it with polarization-entangled photons, detecting a single pair per setting pair.
eli5.matters: Removes an idealisation in Bell tests and is directly useful when calibration drifts, as in superconducting Bell experiments.
eli5.caveat: Loopholes are not the focus; it relaxes a technical assumption rather than closing locality or detection loopholes.

2611.16401.title: Probing the extreme quantum violation of the Leggett-Garg inequality
2611.16401.abstract: The Leggett-Garg (LG) inequalities were formulated for testing the incompatibility between the classical worldview of macrorealism and quantum theory. By analogy with the Tsirelson bound for Bell inequalities, the maximal quantum violation of LG inequalities is commonly referred to as the temporal Tsirelson bound (TTB). Nevertheless, several studies have claimed that, unlike the Tsirelson bound, the TTB can be exceeded within quantum theory. In particular, by employing degeneracy-breaking measurement in [\href{ https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.113.050401}{Phys. Rev. Lett. \textbf{113}, 050401 (2014)}] and by using the superposition of unitaries in [\href{https://doi.org/10.1103/vydp-9qqq}{Phys. Rev. Lett. \textbf{135}, 220202 (2025)}], it is argued that the TTB can be violated. In this work, we critically examine the reasoning underlying these purported TTB violations and show that the corresponding arguments suffer from conceptual shortcomings. We further show that once these conceptual issues are addressed appropriately, the macrorealist bound of LG inequality reaches the algebraic maximum, and hence no violation of the TTB is obtained. In particular, we demonstrate that the proposed TTB violations rely on frameworks that go beyond the standard LG framework, and therefore are of no relevance for testing the incompatibility between macrorealism and quantum theory.
2611.16401.why: Argues claimed violations of the temporal Tsirelson bound for Leggett-Garg rely on changed measurements and do not breach the bound.

eli5.plain: Checks claims that quantum mechanics can beat its own maximum for time-correlation tests, and argues they do not.
eli5.how: Re-analyses degeneracy-breaking and superposition-of-unitaries schemes to show they alter the measurement scenario.
eli5.matters: Leggett-Garg tests are run on superconducting qubits; knowing the true quantum maximum matters for interpreting them.
eli5.caveat: A critique of specific proposals; authors of those papers may contest the operational framing.

2611.13900.title: Correlations carried and controlled by coupled non-Markovian environments
2611.13900.abstract: An environment can retain quantum information and carry it between spatially separated systems. Describing the combined influence of these processes requires a treatment of both environmental memory and spatial correlations. Here, we formulate a local hierarchy of pure states for quantum systems coupled to spatially correlated, non-Markovian environments whose modes themselves exchange excitations. We use this method to describe the reduced spin dynamics of a chain of locally coupled Rabi spin--cavity pairs motivated by cavity-QED implementations, where photon hopping in the eliminated cavity environment generates correlations and entanglement between otherwise isolated spins. Monitoring intermediate cavities and feeding their measurement records back onto the corresponding spins further enhances correlations between endpoint spins that receive no direct feedback. The delayed response when feedback starts, and continued entanglement growth after it stops, support a mechanism in which coherent environmental dynamics carry the effects of earlier feedback to the endpoint spins. Finally, tensor-network simulations of XXZ and Heisenberg chains show how environmental transport changes many-body correlation patterns. These results show how coupled environments and local feedback can control correlations between distant spins. We provide a numerically exact stochastic pure-state framework for simulating these processes, opening up avenues to explore the coherent and dissipative control of interacting non-Markovian many-body systems.
2611.13900.why: Monitoring intermediate cavities and feeding back on spins boosts entanglement between endpoint spins that get no feedback, in a non-Markovian chain.

eli5.plain: A theory method for spins coupled through a chain of cavities that remember the past, showing measurement and feedback in the middle can entangle the ends.
eli5.how: A local hierarchy of pure states handles both bath memory and spatial correlations; measurement records from middle cavities steer neighbouring spins.
eli5.matters: Chains of resonators with qubits are native to circuits, and the feedback scheme maps directly onto measured-and-fed-back microwave modes.
eli5.caveat: Numerical method on modest chains; efficiency and detector requirements are idealised.

2611.15021.title: Reducing TLS Losses in Superconducting Circuits Using Solid Neon
2611.15021.abstract: Two level systems (TLSs) are a major source of loss in superconducting devices, limiting the performance of qubits, detectors, and resonators. These defects arise from a range of sources, including surface oxides, crystal defects, as well as fabrication residues which are often difficult to remove. Using NbTiN coplanar waveguide resonators, we show that depositing and subsequently removing a solid neon film can significantly improve device performance. Analysis of the temperature and power dependence indicates that this enhancement arises from reduced TLS dissipation, which we attribute to the redistribution and removal of surface contaminants during neon deposition and evaporation. Atomic force microscopy images of contaminated hexagonal boron nitride flakes before and after neon exposure show that neon treatment can redistribute and remove surface residues. These results demonstrate a simple, non-destructive approach for mitigating TLS losses in superconducting devices and other sensitive materials that cannot withstand aggressive cleaning processes.
2611.15021.why: Depositing and evaporating a solid neon film measurably reduces TLS loss in NbTiN resonators by cleaning surface residues.

eli5.plain: Frosting a chip with solid neon and then boiling it off cleans the surface enough to make resonators less lossy.
eli5.how: Neon condensation and evaporation redistributes and removes contaminants; power and temperature dependence attribute the improvement to fewer two-level defects.
eli5.matters: A cheap, in-situ, non-chemical cleaning step could help qubit coherence.
eli5.caveat: Shown on resonators, not qubits; the gain's size and durability across thermal cycles are uncertain.

2611.17295.title: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation
2611.17295.abstract: Particle creation in time-dependent quantum fields is a central phenomenon in early-universe cosmology, yet it remains experimentally inaccessible in its original context. We show theoretically that superconducting circuits based on a waveguide-like transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs can provide a direct analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe in conformal time. The mode equation of the circuit reduces to the Weber equation, the same equation governing cosmological particle creation in a radiation-dominated background, admitting an exact solution in terms of parabolic cylinder functions and an exponentially suppressed particle spectrum. We analyse the conditions under which the analogy holds, which require a compromise between the duration of the pulse, the uniformity of the modulation and the symmetry of the SQUIDs, and show that dissipation does not erase the cosmological signal. We use the anomalous moment of each mode as a witness of the Bogoliubov mixing: it vanishes for any thermal state and survives dissipation, and, together with the photon number, it certifies squeezing, and with the purity of the state, it identifies whether the pairs created from the vacuum dominate.
2611.17295.why: A SQUID-loaded transmission line under a flux pulse maps exactly onto particle creation in a radiation-dominated universe, with parabolic-cylinder solutions.

eli5.plain: They show a superconducting line whose properties are changed quickly can mimic how the early universe created particles from vacuum.
eli5.how: Pulsing the SQUIDs changes the line's speed of light in time; the mode equation becomes the same Weber equation as for a scalar field in an expanding universe, giving pairs of microwave photons from vacuum.
eli5.matters: It is a dynamical-Casimir-style squeezing source with an exactly solvable spectrum, a clean benchmark for parametric photon-pair generation in SQUID arrays.
eli5.caveat: Only a proposal; the analogy needs uniform SQUIDs and a carefully shaped pulse, and the predicted signal is exponentially suppressed.

2611.10687.title: Hidden Coherence and Controlled Quasihole Motion in a Fermionic Laughlin State on a Superconducting Quantum Processor
2611.10687.abstract: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states support fractionalized excitations and geometric phases, yet experimentally resolving the many-body coherence encoded in their wave functions remains challenging. Here, we prepare a three-electron $ν=1/3$ Laughlin state on the Haldane sphere using seven superconducting qubits and reconstruct its many-body density matrix. Through Read's composite-boson construction, we reveal vortex-dressed coherence that remains appreciable over a larger separation range than electron coherence. The extended profile is suppressed in a Fock-diagonal reference constructed from the measured populations, demonstrating its dependence on off-diagonal many-body coherence. We further prepare a one-flux-added quasihole and characterize its fractional charge response against finite-size benchmarks. Controlled quasihole motion yields an effective geometric-phase signature from the reconstructed dominant-eigenstate trajectory. These complementary measurements provide microscopic access to the coherent structure and quasihole response of a finite fermionic Laughlin state, demonstrating an experimental route to probing strongly correlated FQH wave functions on programmable quantum processors.
2611.10687.why: Seven qubits prepare a three-electron Laughlin state, reconstruct its density matrix and move a quasihole to extract a geometric phase.

eli5.plain: They built a tiny fractional quantum Hall state on a qubit chip and verified the hidden many-body coherence that makes it special.
eli5.how: Full tomography plus a composite-boson analysis reveals off-diagonal correlations; adding flux creates a quasihole that is then moved around.
eli5.matters: Shows small superconducting processors can probe topological-state features directly.
eli5.caveat: Three electrons are far from the thermodynamic limit; signatures are compared to finite-size benchmarks.

2611.15898.title: Superradiant photon bunching in nanolasers: from a polarization-order hierarchy of the master equation to Dicke Markov chains
2611.15898.abstract: In nanolasers, a few to a few hundred quantum emitters share a single mode of light. Coupled identically to the mode, the emitters do not radiate independently but form collective bright and dark states, producing superradiant bursts and strongly bunched photon statistics below the laser threshold. We investigate to what extent this behavior can be understood as random jumps between collective Dicke states. From the laser master equation, we derive a hierarchy of models defined by the polarization order, i.e., the number of photons involved in the coherence between the emitters and the light, and include the coherence to various orders. With all of the coherences eliminated, we obtain a Dicke Markov chain, a stochastic jump process over the photon number and the Dicke states, in which collective effects enter only through enhanced or suppressed transition rates. It predicts superthermal bunching and a strong even--odd dependence on the emitter number. It recovers about 80\% of the bunching in the most coherent regime, where conventional rate equations predict no superthermal bunching. Keeping the first polarization order, i.e., the optical polarization, and eliminating the second order, i.e., the two-photon coherences, yields a population-polarization model, which recovers the bunching of the full master equation almost perfectly. This hierarchy of polarization orders is an alternative to the cumulant expansion and, unlike it, recovers the master equation at the highest order. As a numerically exact reference, a symmetry-reduced master equation extends the simulation range all the way to 34 (24) emitters below (above) threshold. The Dicke Markov chain can be solved directly for hundreds of emitters and sampled for thousands of emitters, further extending the range of numerical methods. We compare the numerical performance of the methods in detail to guide the choice of technique.
2611.15898.why: Derives a hierarchy from the laser master equation down to a Dicke Markov chain that captures superthermal bunching in nanolasers.

eli5.plain: Explains why a few emitters sharing one cavity mode give bursty, strongly bunched light, as random jumps between collective states.
eli5.how: Coherences between emitters and light are kept to a chosen photon order; eliminating them all gives a simple stochastic model with enhanced and suppressed rates.
eli5.matters: The same few-emitter, one-mode collective physics appears with transmon ensembles in a resonator, and the model is an intuitive g2 predictor.
eli5.caveat: Theory; which order is needed for quantitative agreement depends on parameters.

2611.17906.title: Indefinite causal order with definite Bohmian trajectories for the quantum switch
2611.17906.abstract: We analyze the notion of indefinite causal order (ICO) from the standpoint of the deterministic de Broglie--Bohm theory, based on the notion of trajectories in configuration space. More precisely, we study the physics of the quantum switch (QS) interferometer within a Bohmian framework and show how the notion of causality is preserved in this approach. Furthermore, we investigate device-independent certification and causal inequalities applied to an entangled quantum system, and show that in this regime too, the notions of trajectories and of a strict causal order are perfectly preserved.
2611.17906.why: de Broglie–Bohm trajectories for the quantum switch keep a definite causal order even when causal inequalities are violated.

eli5.plain: In the pilot-wave picture, the 'indefinite order' device always has a definite order underneath.
eli5.how: Modelling the switch interferometer with Bohmian trajectories, they track which operation each particle actually passes first.
eli5.matters: Shows indefinite causal order is interpretation-dependent language, not an observer-independent fact.
eli5.caveat: Bohmian accounts reproduce quantum predictions by construction; the result adds no testable difference.

2611.17268.title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
2611.17268.abstract: Memory effects in open quantum systems do not by themselves imply quantum memory, since non-Markovian dynamics can often be reproduced by classical-memory models. Known criteria certify the presence of quantum memory in the environment by comparing the evolution of the system at two different times. We show that quantum memory can remain hidden from all such pairwise tests and become detectable only when three or more times are considered jointly. We derive an analytical three-time witness and use it to certify quantum memory in a minimal qubit example in which every pair of times has a classical-memory explanation, thus establishing a strict hierarchy of quantum memory effects. Genuine multi-time quantum memory does not rely on fine-tuned time-dependent Hamiltonians or gate-based evolution. We experimentally demonstrate the hierarchy of quantum memory in a time-continuous realization on a superconducting-qubit platform with time-independent couplings.
2611.17268.why: Shows quantum memory in an environment can hide from every two-time test and appear only in a three-time witness, demonstrated experimentally.

eli5.plain: They find a kind of quantum memory in a qubit's surroundings that you can only detect by looking at three moments in time together, never two.
eli5.how: A three-time witness compares joint statistics against all classical-memory models; they build an example where every pair of times has a classical explanation but the triple does not, and realise it in continuous time on hardware.
eli5.matters: Non-Markovian baths are what we fight in circuits; this tells you pairwise noise characterisation can miss genuinely quantum environment memory.
eli5.caveat: The demonstration is a minimal engineered example; how often real TLS or cavity baths show this hierarchy is not addressed.

2611.14968.title: Nitride crystalline barrier epitaxial SIS Josephson junctions by MBE
2611.14968.abstract: Superconductor-insulator-superconductor Josephson junctions with crystalline tunnel barriers have remained elusive by epitaxial techniques such as MOCVD or MBE that produce the junction materials and devices powering today's electronic and photonic systems like transistors and lasers. Here, we overcome the key materials hurdle to realize the first functional nitride crystalline barrier Josephson junctions by MBE. Despite an AlN barrier thickness of approximately 4.5 nm, the NbN/AlN/NbN trilayers exhibit coherent Josephson tunneling with critical current densities of approximately 17 A/cm2, an IcRn product of approximately 2.5 mV, and a superconducting gap voltage of approximately 3.7 mV with a BCS-like gap evolution with temperature. Hysteretic current-voltage characteristics and Fraunhofer current modulation with magnetic field establish underdamped SIS Josephson behavior. The realization of crystalline barrier Josephson junctions by MBE opens the doors to a richer materials palette with alloys and superlattice electrodes and tunnel barriers, as well as potential monolithic integration of superconducting quantum circuits with active electronic and photonic devices such as HEMTs and lasers.
2611.14968.why: First MBE-grown NbN/AlN/NbN junctions with crystalline barriers show clean underdamped SIS Josephson behaviour.

eli5.plain: They grew a fully crystalline superconducting junction by molecular-beam epitaxy, something long sought.
eli5.how: Epitaxial nitride trilayers give Fraunhofer patterns and BCS-like gaps consistent with ideal tunnelling.
eli5.matters: Crystalline barriers could eliminate the amorphous-oxide defects behind TLS loss in qubits.
eli5.caveat: Only DC junction data; no qubit coherence measured, and critical current density is low.

2611.18413.title: Number fluctuations and particle loss in Dicke superradiance
2611.18413.abstract: Dicke superradiance, the collective spontaneous emission of identical quantum emitters into a common reservoir, produces a burst with a characteristic delay $t_{\mathrm{SR}}$ and a peak intensity that scales quadratically with the emitter number $N$. This strong dependence makes the burst sensitive to how many emitters actually participate. In experiments, however, this number is rarely fixed: it fluctuates between preparations and decreases during emission through atom loss. Here we extend the analytical treatment of superradiance to variable emitter numbers using the Schwinger-boson mapping of the collective spin onto two bosonic modes. In this formulation, collective decay annihilates an atom in the excited-state mode and creates one in the ground-state mode. We find that number fluctuations enhance emission and that the ensemble-averaged emission trace encodes the initial number distribution. We show how to reconstruct second-order correlations from photon counting with finite detection efficiency and temporal resolution, even when the full distribution cannot be resolved. For atom loss at rate $r$, we derive exact results for the population dynamics and show that the peak intensity scaling is governed by the single scaling variable $g_{\mathrm{r}}=r t_{\mathrm{SR}}$. The peak remains quadratic in $N$ for $g_{\mathrm{r}}<1$, follows logarithmically corrected subquadratic power laws for $g_{\mathrm{r}}>1$, and crosses over to linear scaling under strong loss with $g_{\mathrm{r}}\gg1$.
2611.18413.why: Number fluctuations and atom loss enhance Dicke superradiance, and the averaged burst encodes the initial number distribution.

eli5.plain: Shows how not knowing exactly how many atoms take part changes a superradiant flash, and that the flash shape reveals the atom-number distribution.
eli5.how: Mapping the collective spin to two bosonic modes lets them handle variable emitter number and loss analytically.
eli5.matters: Superradiance with qubit arrays is accessible in circuits, where effective emitter number varies with detuning and loss.
eli5.caveat: Analytic model assumes identical emitters and a single collective channel.

2611.14583.title: Circuit-aware protection against burst errors in lattice surgery
2611.14583.abstract: Large-scale quantum computing will require logical operations protected against high-energy impacts that disturb many superconducting qubits at once. Gap engineering suppresses relaxation induced by these impacts, but protecting only a subset of qubits requires choosing where that protection is placed. During lattice surgery, measurements change as patches merge and split, exposing different ancillas and temporal boundaries to burst errors. Here we compare three static protection layouts for a simulated lattice-surgery CNOT, matching the numbers of protected ancillas and the X:Z check-type splits. At distance 9, protecting the check type measured during each merge reduces burst-induced excess risk by $38^{+6}_{-5}\%$ relative to a deep geometric band under correlated background matching, without giving the decoder the impact parameters. We attribute this difference to report errors at temporal boundaries and ancilla faults propagating to data, which interact to increase the excess risk of a shallow band. We also find that the typed layout reaches the shallow-band reference risk with an estimated $49^{+2}_{-14}$ fewer protected ancillas. At distance 13, the advantage is not resolved under oracle decoding, and a five-round burst cap reverses the shallow-band ordering. These results indicate how the measurements of a logical circuit can guide protection placement within the simulated decoder and burst-duration regimes tested here.
2611.14583.why: Placing gap-engineered protection on the check type measured during each merge cuts cosmic-ray burst risk in lattice surgery by ~38%.

eli5.plain: When only some qubits can be shielded from radiation bursts, which ones you pick matters during logical operations.
eli5.how: Simulated lattice-surgery CNOTs compare protection layouts; protecting the stabilisers measured at merge time works best.
eli5.matters: Burst errors are a real limit for superconducting QEC, and partial protection is the practical option.
eli5.caveat: Simulation with a specific burst model; hardware validation is absent.

2611.10915.title: Bias-free superconducting microwave nonreciprocity from a passive nonlinear resonator
2611.10915.abstract: Routing microwave tones in a nonreciprocal fashion in a superconducting chip usually requires an external bias, commonly in the form of static magnetic fields, pump tones or temporal modulation. Here we demonstrate microwave nonreciprocity in a bias-free, passive platform, a single nonlinear superconducting resonator patterned in one film without Josephson junctions. Unequal coupling with the two feeding ports makes its nonlinear resonance shift direction-dependent, and its sharp Fano lineshape converts this asymmetric response into a large transmission contrast when excited from opposite directions. Our niobium nitride (NbN) device reaches a directional contrast of 53.0 dB at an insertion loss of 4.6 dB, and it exceeds 20 dB over 9.7 MHz. Time-resolved measurements show that the device routes pulses from 2 us to 1 ms with more than 30 dB of contrast and switches within a few microseconds. Made with the same technology as superconducting amplifiers, such bias-free nonreciprocal components could simplify the on-chip routing of strong pump and control tones in quantum processors
2611.10915.why: A single junction-free NbN nonlinear resonator gives 53 dB passive, bias-free nonreciprocity with 4.6 dB insertion loss.

eli5.plain: A one-layer superconducting resonator lets microwaves through in one direction but not the other, with no magnet or pump.
eli5.how: Unequal coupling to the two ports makes the nonlinear frequency shift direction dependent, and a sharp Fano lineshape turns this into large contrast.
eli5.matters: Compact isolation without ferrites would help readout chains.
eli5.caveat: Nonlinear isolators depend on signal power, so it does not act on few-photon quantum signals the way a circulator does.

2611.13084.title: Field-induced phase-matching in Josephson traveling wave parametric amplifiers
2611.13084.abstract: Superconducting Josephson traveling wave parametric amplifiers (JTWPAs) enable broadband, quantum-limited amplification of weak microwave signals. JTWPAs are essential for the single-shot readout of superconducting qubits, broadband vacuum squeezing, or the generation of microwave cluster states. Phase-matching between signal and pump modes in such JTWPAs represents a major engineering challenge, which is typically solved by integrating resonators in a nonlinear medium in order to tailor electromagnetic dispersion relations and achieve a broadband, high-gain amplification. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a phase-matching approach using a homogeneous nonlinear medium based on Josephson elements by exploiting a magnetic field inhomogeneity. We show how the latter may lead to the sign reversal of the 3-wave mixing nonlinearity and stabilization of the parametric amplification. We envision this technique as a viable alternative to conventional phase-matching approaches.
2611.13084.why: Uses a deliberate magnetic-field gradient to flip the sign of three-wave mixing and phase-match a homogeneous Josephson travelling-wave amplifier.

eli5.plain: They make a broadband quantum-limited microwave amplifier work without the usual built-in resonators, by using an uneven magnetic field.
eli5.how: In a uniform chain of Josephson elements, a field gradient changes the sign of the three-wave-mixing nonlinearity along the line, which keeps signal and pump in step.
eli5.matters: Simpler travelling-wave amplifiers matter for readout and for broadband squeezing and microwave cluster states.
eli5.caveat: Gain, bandwidth and added noise relative to resonantly phase-matched devices are not established from the abstract.

2611.14622.title: Squeezed Light Generation by Cooper Pair Recombination in a Superconductor-Semiconductor Structure
2611.14622.abstract: We theoretically demonstrate squeezed light generation in a compact, electrically driven device utilizing the nonlinear light-matter interaction of Cooper-pair recombination in a hybrid superconductorsemiconductor structure. On the basis of second-order perturbation theory, we developed an effective Hamiltonian which incorporates the electronic component of the interaction as a photon coupling strength coefficient, enabling a model to describe the quadrature squeezing effect of Cooper-pair recombination on the photonic state. We find the squeezing strength to be proportional to the superconducting energy gap squared and device length, as well as increasing with applied voltage. For practical device length, materials and voltage bias, we calculated squeezing values comparable to those of existing squeezed light generation methods when operating below the critical temperature. This theoretically developed concept shows viability for electrically pumped squeezed light generation and can pave the way towards realization of squeezing in compact integrated structures.
2611.14622.why: Proposes electrically driven squeezed light from Cooper-pair recombination in a superconductor-semiconductor junction, scaling with gap squared.

eli5.plain: A proposed chip that makes squeezed light when Cooper pairs recombine into photons in a semiconductor.
eli5.how: Second-order perturbation theory gives an effective two-photon Hamiltonian whose strength grows with gap, length and voltage.
eli5.matters: A superconducting-physics route to nonclassical light that might interface with superconducting hardware.
eli5.caveat: Purely theoretical with optimistic parameters; losses and competing emission are not experimentally constrained.

2611.16563.title: Noise-Protected Superconducting Qudits from Higher-Harmonic Josephson Junctions
2611.16563.abstract: Qudits, which generalize qubits to $d$ levels, store more information per circuit element than qubits. As with qubits, however, their sensitivity to noise must be overcome before they can be used for fault-tolerant quantum computing. Here we show that, by exploiting the second harmonic of the current--phase relation, a superconducting loop of three Josephson junctions can host qutrits strongly protected against relaxation, while dephasing limits their coherence. When the second harmonic is positive, a simple loop with a small asymmetry between the junctions provides a tunable, symmetry-protected qutrit. When it is negative, a protected qutrit can be realized by adding a small symmetry-breaking term, such as a weak Josephson diode effect. The two designs involve different trade-offs: the first has an exact charge selection rule, whereas the second is nearly insensitive to charge noise and its quasiparticle errors can be corrected. The preferable choice therefore depends on the materials used. Both require a sizable second harmonic to begin with, and we identify altermagnetic Josephson junctions as a candidate platform. Finally, microscopic calculations show that a gate voltage selects the sign of the second harmonic in these junctions, although gate-voltage noise then becomes the leading source of dephasing. These findings establish the sign of the second harmonic as a design principle for protected superconducting qudits.
2611.16563.why: Second-harmonic Josephson terms let a three-junction loop host qutrits protected against relaxation, with two designs trading charge sensitivity.

2611.11468.title: Quantum State Reconstruction from Sklar-Type Relational Data
2611.11468.abstract: Sklar's theorem in classical probability theory rigorously separates the marginal statistics of a joint probability distribution from its dependence structure data. We apply this perspective to the context-dependent classical probability tables induced by the Born rule for a quantum state. For each Born probability table of a given quantum state, we discard the marginal statistics of the individual parties, retaining only the relational data among them. Yet we prove that, when these classical relational data are collected over all contexts, the nontrivial quantum compatibility constraints inherent in quantum mechanics suffice to reconstruct any irreducible multiqubit quantum state itself. This means that the local information of the subsystems, discarded table by table, is fully recovered. We call this quantum-state reconstruction from Sklar-type relational data.
2611.11468.why: Relational copula data from Born tables across all contexts suffice to reconstruct any irreducible multiqubit state.

eli5.plain: Even after throwing away every local outcome statistic, the correlation structure alone pins down the quantum state.
eli5.how: Applying Sklar's copula decomposition table by table, quantum compatibility constraints across contexts restore the marginals.
eli5.matters: A relational reading of the state: correlations carry the full content.
eli5.caveat: Mathematical; physical reading beyond tomography is suggestive.

2611.12576.title: All-to-all connectivity via adiabatic ZZ interactions in a superconducting flux qubit processor
2611.12576.abstract: Scalable superconducting quantum processors would benefit from high qubit connectivity, yet existing architectures connect neighbouring qubits via tunable couplers, which introduce substantial wiring and control overhead. Here, we propose a baseband-driven adiabatic ZZ gate that entangles any selected pair in a register of flux qubits coupled via a common cavity. The qubits stay dc-biased at their flux sweet spot. Strong drives applied selectively through local flux lines, at frequencies far below the qubit transitions, adiabatically tilt the quantization axes and generate an effective longitudinal ZZ interaction. The strength of the coupling is tunable and controlled by the amplitudes and relative phase of the drives rather than by any resonance condition. Numerical simulations give coherent gate errors below $10^{-4}$ over broad ranges of drive frequency, with comparable fidelities for two simultaneous gates in a four-qubit register. The protocol is robust against frequency fluctuations and remains effective even when many qubits are coupled to the cavity.
2611.12576.why: Baseband drives tilt flux-qubit quantization axes to create tunable all-to-all ZZ gates through a shared cavity, simulated below 1e-4 error.

2611.10295.title: Dynamical Light-Matter Coupling with Protected Superconducting Oscillators
2611.10295.abstract: Superconducting circuits hosting long-lived bosonic modes are an excellent platform for emulating the dynamics of light and matter and exploiting them for quantum information processing. The space of accessible dynamics is greatly extended by introducing the frequency tunability of artificial atoms, whereby the interactions with the light field of a microwave cavity can be modified on demand. However, using external flux bias to control the frequency of transmons introduces significant losses to coupled cavities, reducing their single-photon lifetimes to a few tens of $μ$s. These imperfections compromise the usefulness of the bosonic mode, which loses its ability to store and manipulate the quantum information of many-photon states. This thesis investigates the issue and demonstrates how to enhance the flux control of microwave cavities without compromising protection. Several hardware solutions were explored, including off-plane remote flux sources routed by a magnetic hose, and lithographically printed on-chip lines equipped with multiple stages of filtering. These developments equip the systems with broadband flux control and photon lifetimes of several hundred $μ$s. They enable the real-time manipulation of the two central parameters of the Rabi model: detuning and coupling strength. This flexibility translates into operational primitives of interest, such as the calibration of nonlinearities to different interaction regimes, the activation of parametric resonances with adjustable coupling strengths, and the use of number-selective transmon-cavity transitions for qudit state preparation and control. These results lay the groundwork for exploring richer synthetic light-matter systems, controlling cavities with more complex nonlinear circuits, and engineering driven-dissipative systems with applications in quantum computation and sensing.
2611.10295.why: Thesis demonstrating flux-tunable transmons coupled to long-lived 3D cavities without the usual flux-line damage to cavity lifetimes.

eli5.plain: A thesis on how to tune an artificial atom's frequency quickly without spoiling the long-lived microwave box it talks to.
eli5.how: Several hardware strategies route flux control so that it no longer opens loss channels in the protected cavity, keeping photon lifetimes long.
eli5.matters: Tunable light–matter coupling with high-Q bosonic modes enables on-demand photon-number manipulation and dynamic coupling experiments.
eli5.caveat: A thesis compiles results; the novel parts and the achieved lifetimes need checking against the papers it draws on.

2611.14637.title: A discrete realization of the boundary sine-Gordon model and the Schmid transition
2611.14637.abstract: The phase diagram of the boundary sine-Gordon model (bsG), or equivalently of the resistively shunted Josephson junction, has been the subject of recent debate. We introduce a discrete model that reproduces exactly the properties of the bsG model and can be simulated extremely efficiently using cluster Monte Carlo algorithms. This enables us to explore a broad range of parameters and compute the complete universal crossover between the weak- and strong-tunneling regimes. We establish the self-duality of the model and unambiguously identify the vertical line of critical fixed points characteristic of the Schmid transition, recovering the conformal field theory predictions along this line with high accuracy. We further clarify the essential distinctions between the Schmid and Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions. Our results definitively establish the existence and nature of the Schmid transition and demonstrate the validity of the Schmid-Bulgadaev scenario.
2611.14637.why: Cluster Monte Carlo on an exact discrete model maps the full Schmid transition line of the shunted Josephson junction, settling its existence.

2611.13791.title: Eigenmode and field imaging of a compact superconducting resonator array
2611.13791.abstract: Superconducting resonator arrays can tailor the photonic environment for quantum information processing, but conventional port-based microwave spectroscopy alone does not resolve the rich spatial structure of their modes. Here, we apply laser scanning microscopy (LSM) and nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center magnetometry to a two-dimensional superconducting resonator array consisting of 33 lumped-element resonators arranged in a honeycomb lattice hosting topological edge states. We demonstrate the complementarity of the two techniques: LSM images the eigenmodes, while NV magnetometry maps the local microwave magnetic field amplitude. Using this spatial information, we experimentally validate that the realized lattice matches the design, we image the topological edge state and measure its sublattice polarization, and place an upper bound of $\approx0.3\%$ on the relative on-site frequency disorder in the lattice. Our work establishes a combined spatial characterization approach for compact superconducting resonator arrays with applications in hybrid spin--superconducting quantum systems.
2611.13791.why: Laser scanning and NV magnetometry image eigenmodes and topological edge states of a 33-site superconducting honeycomb resonator lattice.

eli5.plain: They took pictures of how microwaves sit inside a chip-scale lattice of resonators, including modes that live only on its edge.
eli5.how: Laser heating locally perturbs the resonators to map each mode, while diamond NV centres measure the local microwave magnetic field.
eli5.matters: Spatial imaging verifies photonic lattices used for synthetic light–matter physics and bounds disorder to about 0.3%.
eli5.caveat: The techniques are invasive or slow and work on resonators alone, not with qubits in place.

2611.13175.title: Quantized memory of measurement records near the light cone of quantum circuits
2611.13175.abstract: Quantum processors now measure qubits in the middle of a circuit, and the stream of outcomes is the raw output of error correction, measurement-based state preparation and monitored dynamics. For a scrambling circuit, predicting the statistics of this stream is as hard as simulating the processor, so there is no exact reference to check it against once the device outgrows classical simulation. We show that near the light cone the problem becomes exactly solvable, for any two-qubit gate. In a brickwork circuit with one polarized qubit in a maximally mixed background, measurements along the edge of the light cone form a two-state Markov chain, and measurements $d$ sites inside the edge are generated by $\lfloor d/2\rfloor+1$ qubits that move with it, while the rest of the chain, however large, acts on them as a memoryless bath. The memory of the record is therefore quantized, one bit on the edge and at most one more for every site of displacement, a bound that generic gates attain. The same causal structure determines which hardware noise the record can see, removes that sensitivity at no gate cost, and yields a tomography-free witness of dual-unitarity. On a 156-qubit superconducting processor, a demonstration with its analysis specified in advance finds the predicted memory one and two sites inside the light cone, and none where the theory forbids it. This gives dynamic circuits an exact reference at any system size, and shows that the collision models of open-system theory arise exactly inside chaotic dynamics.
2611.13175.why: Mid-circuit measurement records near a scrambling circuit's light cone become an exactly solvable Markov chain with quantized memory.

2611.14358.title: High-Speed Control of a Fluxonium Qubit via Picosecond Pulses from Josephson Digital Circuits
2611.14358.abstract: We develop a control strategy for fluxonium qubits based on picosecond single-flux-quantum (SFQ) pulses generated by Josephson digital circuits. A major challenge is that SFQ protocols originally designed for transmon control become inefficient for low-frequency fluxonium. In this regime, the asymmetry of flux and charge couplings leads either to excessive leakage or excessively long gate times. We show that this limitation can be overcome by two complementary protocols. The first protocol employs high-frequency SFQ pulse packets applied through the flux channel, offering a simple, analytically transparent, and robust approach for high-fidelity single-qubit control. The second protocol combines phase-shifted flux and charge pulse sequences to enhance the resonant drive and reduce the gate duration. Multilevel simulations demonstrate single-qubit gate fidelities above $99.99\%$; the simpler protocol remains robust under moderate variations of qubit parameters and flux bias, while the combined protocol preserves high fidelity while substantially accelerating the gate. These results establish SFQ-based cryogenic control as a realistic route to fast, accurate, and scalable manipulation of fluxonium qubits.
2611.14358.why: SFQ pulse protocols via flux, or combined flux and charge, give simulated >99.99% fluxonium gates despite the low qubit frequency.

2611.16794.title: Hong$-$Ou$-$Mandel-like interference between two independent narrowband thermal states
2611.16794.abstract: Narrowband photonic sources are promising candidates in quantum networks for a direct interface with atomic quantum memories. However, building a large-scale quantum network requires many indistinguishable sources, and matching the frequencies of independent narrowband sources is generally challenging. Here, we propose a method to measure the frequency difference between two narrowband light sources in the single-photon power regime by studying Hong$-$Ou$-$Mandel-like (HOM) interference between thermal states. Our results show that the absolute value of the frequency difference can be extracted from the temporal coincidence counts, and these results agree well with our theoretical model. We also demonstrate that the beat signal of the HOM-like interference between two thermal states has a similar oscillation profile to the HOM interference between two heralded single-photon sources, confirming that this method can be used to find the zero detuning of two heralded single-photon sources.
2611.16794.why: Hong-Ou-Mandel-like interference of two narrowband thermal sources measures their frequency difference at single-photon power.

eli5.plain: They use two-photon interference between ordinary thermal light sources to tell how far apart their colours are.
eli5.how: Coincidence counts after a beamsplitter beat at the frequency difference, with the same profile as heralded-photon HOM.
eli5.matters: A cheap calibration of source matching, the problem behind waveform adaptation for networks.
eli5.caveat: Thermal-state visibility is limited to 50%, so it is a diagnostic, not a source.

2611.10282.title: Experimental visual quantum state discrimination
2611.10282.abstract: Almost all solutions to vision tasks $\unicode{x2014}$ offered by nature and technology alike $\unicode{x2014}$ rely on capturing an image using a lens or a similar optical instrument, followed by computational analysis by neurons of a brain or a digital computer. This approach is inherently suboptimal in photon-limited and noisy conditions, where critical information is irreversibly lost at the measurement stage. We address this gap by introducing AI-driven optimization of quantum measurements on the incoming photons, learning how to extract the maximum possible information for a given computer vision task from each incoming photon. The trained measurement consists of a diffractive optical neural network (DONN) followed by a detector array. We train the DONN with a quantum information-theoretic objective that maximizes the rate at which the discrimination error decays as photons accumulate. The resulting measurement achieves exponentially lower error than both direct imaging and a DONN optimized for single-photon discrimination. We validate the advantage in a noiseless setting as well as a photon-counting experiment with an electron-multiplying CCD with the noise corresponding to $10^4$ photons per single signal photon, where the measurement also learns to mitigate the detector noise.
2611.10282.why: Trains a diffractive optical network to perform near-optimal quantum measurements for photon-limited vision tasks.

eli5.plain: A learned optical front-end decides how to measure each photon so an image classification needs fewer photons.
eli5.how: A diffractive network is optimised against a quantum-information error-exponent objective and followed by a detector array.
eli5.matters: The principle—optimise measurement before detection—applies to photon-starved microwave readout too.
eli5.caveat: Demonstrated on simple discrimination tasks; gains over good classical optics may be modest.

2611.12882.title: Chiral waveguide model for error-correctable quantum computation
2611.12882.abstract: We develop a first-principles framework connecting microscopic waveguide scattering to quantum error correction and algorithmic performance. For polarization-encoded single photons interacting with an ensemble of two-level atoms in a chiral waveguide, we derive an effective polarization quantum channel by tracing out the frequency degree of freedom. Using this channel as the physical noise model for a rotated planar code, we observe threshold behavior as the number of atoms $N$ and the atom-waveguide coupling strength $Γ$ are varied. An asymptotic analysis of the microscopic scattering model explains the threshold scaling with $NΓ/σ$, where $σ$ is the photon spectral bandwidth. For identical, lossless atoms with symmetric real coupling and a photon spectrum centered at resonance, the effective noise is strongly biased toward $X$ errors. We then incorporate the resulting logical errors into quantum phase estimation and demonstrate that the noise bias can guide circuit design. In particular, a Hadamard-basis implementation reduces sensitivity to the dominant error, improving algorithmic performance.
2611.12882.why: Derives a polarization error channel from chiral-waveguide scattering off N atoms and finds surface-code thresholds scaling with NΓ/σ.

eli5.plain: Connects how a photon scatters off atoms in a one-way waveguide to whether an error-correcting code built on it would work.
eli5.how: Tracing out frequency gives an effective qubit channel, used as noise for a planar code simulation.
eli5.matters: Useful template for turning waveguide-QED microphysics into QEC numbers, also for microwave photons.
eli5.caveat: Idealised lossless identical atoms; the threshold depends strongly on spectral assumptions.

2611.17562.title: DRAG-Inspired Single Flux Quantum Control of Superconducting Qubits
2611.17562.abstract: Scalable control remains a major challenge for superconducting quantum processors due to the wiring, thermal load, and hardware complexity associated with conventional microwave-based architectures. A framework for qubit control based on Single Flux Quantum (SFQ) digital electronics is presented. For transmon qubits, optimized control sequences are constructed from regular pulse trains framed by arbitrary subsequences (ramps), enabling DRAG-inspired leakage suppression in the discrete SFQ regime through genetic-algorithm optimization. For representative $Y_{π/2}$ gates, the resulting sequences achieve simulated coherent-control infidelities below $10^{-4}$, including leakage from the computational subspace. The objective of the proposed approach is to demonstrate that coherent errors intrinsic to SFQ control can be reduced to a comparable level for a more scalable cryogenic control architecture. Memory requirements are reduced by storing only the optimized ramps, while a modular controller architecture supporting both regular and arbitrary pulse generation is proposed. The logical complexity of this architecture is estimated from the Josephson-junction counts of its constituent SFQ cells. The proposed approach therefore combines low coherent-control error with reduced memory overhead and provides a basis for scalable cryogenic SFQ control architectures.
2611.17562.why: Genetic-algorithm SFQ pulse trains with ramps suppress transmon leakage DRAG-style to simulated infidelities below 1e-4.

2611.14422.title: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers
2611.14422.abstract: Quantum algorithms for machine learning, chemistry, and cryptanalysis often assume coherent access to classical data at negligible physical cost. We instead treat data loading as a hardware process and quantify the dynamic energetic cost of a quantum random access memory (QRAM) query on a superconducting processor. Using the metric-noise-resource framework, we relate query fidelity and power to gate duration, relative two-qubit drive strength, and the distribution of attenuation across a multi-stage refrigerator, while accounting for thermal photons and gate errors. We analyze the linear-depth multiplexer and the noise-resilient bucket-brigade architectures, adapting the latter to a native superconducting gate set and refining its fidelity analysis using the fully decomposed gate schedule. For a representative bucket-brigade QRAM query with a $12$-qubit address register we obtain a query fidelity of $0.969$. The query consumes $3.51\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{J}$ of dynamic energy, corresponding to an average dynamic power of $4.38\,\mathrm{W}$ and a peak of $64.4\,\mathrm{W}$. Our optimization shows that, at fixed target fidelity, the operating point and attenuation profile can change the average power by a factor of two or more.
2611.14422.why: Estimates the energy and cryogenic heat load of a bucket-brigade QRAM query on superconducting hardware.

2611.13799.title: Coherent Optical Readout of Neutral-Atom Qubits via Homodyne Detection of Resonant Fluorescence
2611.13799.abstract: Fast, non-destructive qubit readout is essential for repeated sampling, mid-circuit measurement, and fault-tolerant neutral-atom quantum processing, but camera-based fluorescence detection introduces electronic latency beyond fluorescence-collection time. We propose coherent readout of the state-dependent resonant fluorescence using balanced homodyne detection with photodiodes. An analytic model quantifies the effect of atomic motion on the time-integrated quadrature signal and noise, showing that harmonic motion causes phase averaging while photon recoils produce trajectory-dependent signal fluctuations; the competition between signal accumulation and motion-induced decoherence sets an optimal detection time. Three-dimensional Monte Carlo simulations validate the model and predict state-detection fidelities exceeding 99% within 100 $μ\mathrm{s}$ for experimentally realistic parameters. These results establish the readout conditions and physical constraints for rapid coherent fluorescence readout of neutral-atom qubits.
2611.13799.why: Proposes homodyne detection of resonance fluorescence for >99% neutral-atom readout within 100 μs.

eli5.plain: Read neutral-atom qubits by measuring the wave of scattered light with a photodiode instead of counting photons on a camera.
eli5.how: Balanced homodyne detection integrates the fluorescence quadrature; a model and Monte Carlo include atomic motion.
eli5.matters: Mirrors dispersive homodyne readout in circuits; shows the trade-off between signal and motion-induced dephasing.
eli5.caveat: Simulation only; collection efficiency assumptions drive the fidelity.

2611.14944.title: CSS Circuits: useful quantum circuits that can be simulated with $O(1)$ cost per gate
2611.14944.abstract: "CSS circuits" are quantum circuits generated by $X$, $Z$, $M_X$, $M_Z$, and CNOT gates. Although CSS circuits are extremely restrictive, they can implement important quantum protocols like teleportation, error correction, and entanglement purification. We present a simple CSS circuit simulator that uses $O(1)$ work per gate. The simulator corresponds to a local hidden variable model, so we use Bell inequalities to prove the simulator can't also support Hadamard gates, CZ gates, or S gates. We note that CSS circuits appear ideal for benchmarking quantum error correction in the presence of atom loss errors.
2611.14944.why: CSS circuits admit an O(1)-per-gate local-hidden-variable simulation, and Bell arguments show it cannot include Hadamard.

eli5.plain: A class of error-correction-style circuits can be simulated very cheaply because they never become truly nonlocal.
eli5.how: The simulator is a local hidden variable model; Bell inequalities prove adding Hadamard, CZ or S breaks it.
eli5.matters: Fast QEC benchmarking tool with a clean foundations link.
eli5.caveat: Foundational content is a corollary; main use is simulation.

2611.12876.title: The simulability frontiers of photonic quantum computing
2611.12876.abstract: Estimates of when photonic devices outgrow classical simulation are hard to compare: even for single-photon boson sampling, quoted thresholds range from 50 to 98 photons, as they rest on different tasks and assumptions. We propose as a common unit the time a classical computer needs to draw one sample from the device's exact output distribution, up to floating-point rounding. Only exactness applies equally to every kind of light, since the cost of approximate sampling depends on the accuracy required. The simulability frontier is the device size at which our fastest exact sampler produces one sample per second on a fixed machine; this device size increases with better hardware and algorithms. As the time per sample grows exponentially with the number of detected photons, doubling the machine speed moves the frontier by about one photon, whereas a better algorithm changes the growth rate. We measure the frontier with photonic-engines, an open-source GPU library of exact samplers for single photons, entangled photons from quantum emitters, vacuum-single-photon superpositions and squeezed light. Each sampler is validated against a simulator sharing no code with it.
